title: Erdős Problem #180: Turán Numbers for Graph Families
description: For a finite family F of graphs, does there exist G in F such that ex(n;G) = O(ex(n;F))? Yes for non-bipartite families by Erdős-Stone. Folklore counterexample for infinite families. OPEN.

meta.author: Erdős-Simonovits [ErSi82]
originalContributions: turanNumber: sSup of edge counts in H-free graphs
ExSingle, ExFamily: type aliases for extremal functions ℕ → ℕ
HasDomination: some member has ex(n;G) = O(ex(n;F))
ErdosConjecture180: every finite family has domination

prerequisites: Finset and sSup in Lean 4 / Mathlib

overview.historicalContext: Erdős and Simonovits posed this problem in 1982, building on the foundational work in extremal graph theory. Turán's theorem (1941) gives $\text{ex}(n; K_r) = (1 - 1/(r-1))n^2/2 + O(n)$. The Erdős-Stone theorem (1946) extends this to all non-bipartite $H$: $\text{ex}(n; H) = (1 - 1/(\chi(H)-1))n^2/2 + o(n^2)$, completely resolving the domination question when all family members have $\chi \geq 3$ — the member with smallest chromatic number controls the asymptotics. The difficulty lies in bipartite families, where $\text{ex}(n; H) = o(n^2)$ but the exact growth rates depend on delicate structural properties captured by the Zarankiewicz problem $z(n; s, t)$. The Kővári-Sós-Turán theorem gives $\text{ex}(n; K_{s,t}) = O(n^{2-1/s})$, but matching lower bounds are known only for specific cases, making asymptotic comparisons between different bipartite Turán numbers extremely hard.
overview.problemStatement: For a finite family F of graphs, let ex(n;F) be the maximum edges in an n-vertex F-free graph. Does there always exist G in F such that ex(n;G) = O(ex(n;F))? OPEN.
overview.proofStrategy: The formalization defines ExFamily, ExSingle, HasDomination, and the main conjecture ErdosConjecture180. The non-bipartite case is axiomatized via Erdős-Stone. The folklore counterexample for infinite families demonstrates that finiteness is essential. The summary theorem proves the conjunction of these known results.
keyInsights: The domination property asks if a single forbidden graph controls the family's extremal function
Non-bipartite case resolved by Erdős-Stone: chromatic number determines asymptotics up to o(n²)
The bipartite case is nontrivial due to unknown Zarankiewicz-type bounds
Folklore counterexample for infinite families: star + matching
Finiteness of the family F is essential to the conjecture

sections.title: Turán Numbers
sections.summary: Defines `turanNumber H n` as $\text{ex}(n; H) = \sup\{|E(G)| : |V(G)| = n,\, H \not\subseteq G\}$ via `sSup`. Introduces `ExSingle` and `ExFamily` as type aliases ($\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$) for extremal functions of individual graphs and families.

sections.title: The Domination Property
sections.summary: Defines `HasDomination familyEx memberExs`: $\exists G \in F,\, \exists C > 0,\, \forall n:\; \text{ex}(n;G) \leq C \cdot \text{ex}(n;F)$. This formalizes the Big-O domination condition — a single forbidden graph controls the family's extremal function.

sections.title: The Main Conjecture
sections.summary: Formalizes `ErdosConjecture180`: every finite nonempty family $F$ with $\text{ex}(n;F) \leq \min_{G \in F} \text{ex}(n;G)$ has the domination property. No axiom is provided — this is the OPEN question.

sections.title: Non-Bipartite Case (Erdős-Stone)
sections.summary: Axiomatizes `erdos_stone_domination`: for families where every member has chromatic number $\geq 3$, the Erdős-Stone theorem gives $\text{ex}(n;H) = ((r-2)/(r-1) + o(1))\binom{n}{2}$, so the member with smallest $\chi$ dominates.

sections.title: Bipartite Case Difficulty
sections.summary: Defines `BipartiteCase` (a finite family without domination, which would refute the conjecture). Axiomatizes `folklore_counterexample_infinite`: $F = \{K_{1,n}, M_n\}$ (star + matching) gives $\text{ex}(n;F) \leq 1$ while individual members allow $\Theta(n)$ edges, showing finiteness is essential.

sections.title: Properties
sections.summary: Axiomatizes `family_le_members`: $\text{ex}(n;F) \leq \min_{G \in F} \text{ex}(n;G)$. Forbidding more subgraphs can only reduce the maximum edge count — the defining monotonicity of family Turán numbers.

sections.title: Summary
sections.summary: Proves `erdos_180_summary`: conjunction of non-bipartite domination (Erdős-Stone) and the infinite-family counterexample. The open question is whether domination holds for ALL finite families, especially those containing bipartite graphs where Zarankiewicz-type bounds are imprecise.

conclusion.summary: Erdős Problem #180 asks whether a single forbidden graph always dominates the Turán number of a finite graph family. Resolved for non-bipartite families via Erdős-Stone, but open in general. The folklore counterexample shows finiteness is essential.
conclusion.implications: Resolution would clarify the structure of extremal functions for forbidden graph families, connecting to the Zarankiewicz problem and bipartite Turán theory.
openQuestions: Does domination hold for all finite families?
What happens for families of bipartite graphs?
Can the folklore counterexample be extended to finite families?
How does the answer depend on the structure of the family?

crossReferences.description: Erdős #167 (Tuza's conjecture) also concerns extremal graph theory — packing/covering duality for triangles, connecting to how forbidden subgraph structure controls edge counts
Erdős #1079 studies Turán density in neighborhoods — a local variant of the Turán number questions central to Problem #180
Ramsey theory and extremal graph theory are dual: Ramsey asks when structure must appear, Turán asks how much structure can be avoided — both concern forbidden subgraph thresholds
